title: The effect of spatiotemporal resolution on predictive policing model performance
thesis: Evaluates how varying grid resolution, temporal resolution, and historical time frame affect predictive policing model performance to identify optimal parameter values.
theme_1_justification: Not addressed. The paper does not discuss dual-use, technology transfer, or the economic properties of software/data.
theme_2_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of algorithmic opacity, epistemic authority, surveillance as knowledge production, or democratic deficits.
theme_3_justification: Not addressed. The paper does not conceptualize the city as a programmable system, discuss modulation, or engage with smart city governance beyond technical prediction.
theme_4_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of spatial destruction, home unmaking, urban warfare, or weaponisation of infrastructure.
policy_relevance: None explicitly, but discusses implications for police resource allocation and the trade-off between prediction performance and spatiotemporal resolution.
notes: Paper is a technical empirical study on predictive policing model optimization. Includes an erratum about missing declaration of competing interest, but content unaffected.
